title: Burgundians
capsule: The Burgundians were an East Germanic people who appear in Roman sources from the 3rd century CE, settled on the middle Rhine near Worms. A catastrophic Roman-backed Hun assault c. 436–437 annihilated perhaps 20,000 Burgundians and became the historical kernel of the Nibelungenlied. Survivors were resettled by Aetius in Sapaudia (Savoy) c. 443, and the Burgundians built a kingdom in the Rhône–Saône corridor that reached as far south as Provence. In 534 the Frankish kings Childebert I and Chlothar I conquered and partitioned the Burgundian kingdom, absorbing the Burgundians into the Frankish world.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Written sources attest the Burgundians' Rhine settlement and Sapaudian resettlement; their earlier territorial range before the 5th century is poorly defined.
